requirements.evidence: Pins in .env.example:1,7 and phpunit.xml:22-24; theme config/mail.php:129-135 ('theme' => 'pegafila') with '.button-primary { background-color: #0f7490; }' in pegafila.css; lang/pt_BR.json adds 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address'; routes/web.php:16-33 define password.request/email (throttle:6,1)/reset/update under 'guest' and verification.verify with ['auth','signed','throttle:6,1']; PasswordResetLinkController.php:31-34 ignores broker status and always flashes __(Password::RESET_LINK_SENT); NewPasswordController.php:33-56 validates token/email/PasswordRule::min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers() + confirmed, forceFills password and remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on id/hash mismatch) and redirects '/'. reset-password view has a single email input.

conventions.evidence: Test-first Pest coverage, CHANGELOG.md updated under Added/Changed, PHPDoc on public methods, Bulma markup with labels. Deviation: NewPasswordController.php:33-37 validates three fields inline although conventions ask for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields; the password write is done inline in the controller closure rather than in an app/Actions class (debatable since it is auth, not domain).

security.evidence: No account enumeration (PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-34 identical response; tested in PasswordResetTest 'an unknown address gets the same response'); throttle:6,1 on the POST and on verification; strong password rules; remember_token rotated (NewPasswordController.php:44); signed + auth + EmailVerificationRequest hash/id check; forceFill used only on server-controlled values; all output via {{ }}.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/AccountMailTest.php covers config pins, theme file/color and both rendered notifications (subject, button, greeting, body, sub-copy, absence of English); PasswordResetTest.php covers form rendering, guest-only redirect, sent vs unknown address, validation, 429 throttling, valid reset with event and token rotation, single-use token, invalid token, a dataset for each password rule, confirmation; EmailVerificationTest.php covers success, already verified, wrong hash, other user's id, unsigned link.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, EmailVerificationRequest and built-in notifications; only two lang keys added. Some weight: pegafila.css is a 297-line full copy of the default theme to change the button color, and both auth views duplicate the full HTML head including a CDN fallback ('@else <link ... bulma@0.9.4 ...>').

readability.evidence: Small focused controllers with clear names; explanatory comment at PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-31 on why the broker status is ignored; descriptive Pest test names. Minor: top-level 'const RESET_LINK_SENT' and global function verificationUrl() in test files share the global namespace.

scope.evidence: Diff touches only env/phpunit pins, mail config + theme, two lang keys, the five routes, three controllers, two views, tests and CHANGELOG; no login/registration, layouts, ui.php, SCSS/JS or Docker changes.

issues.explanation: Three-field validation is inline; the conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Both views duplicate the full HTML shell and add a Bulma CDN fallback that is not requested and loads an external stylesheet.
The whole default theme is copied to change the primary button color, adding a large file to maintain.
A global constant and global helper function in Pest files can collide with future test files declaring the same names.

review.summary: The change delivers the pt-BR locale pins, the pegafila mail theme, the missing translation keys, the guest password-reset flow with no account enumeration, and the signed verification route, all with thorough Pest tests and a CHANGELOG entry. Only small issues remain: inline validation where a Form Request is expected, and some duplicated markup/CSS. I would approve with nits.
